items.testName: Conduct Search Engine Discovery and Reconnaissance for Information Leakage
items.description: Use a search engine to search for Network diagrams and Configurations, Credentials, Error message content.
items.tools: Google Hacking, Sitedigger, Shodan, FOCA, Punkspider

items.description: Find the version and type of a running web server to determine known vulnerabilities and the appropriate exploits. Using HTTP header field ordering and Malformed requests test.

items.testName: Review Webserver Metafiles for Information Leakage
items.description: Analyze robots.txt, sitemap.xml and identify < META > Tags from website.
Find applications hosted in the webserver (Virtual hosts/Subdomain), non-standard ports, DNS zone transfers.
items.tools: Webhosting.info, dnsrecon, Nmap, fierce, Recon-ng, Intrigue

items.testName: Review Webpage Comments and Metadata for Information Leakage
items.description: Find sensitive information from webpage comments and Metadata on source code.
Identify from hidden fields, parameters, methods HTTP header analysis.
Map the target application and understand the principal workflows.
Find the type of web application framework/CMS from HTTP headers, Cookies, Source code, Specific files and folders.
Identify the web application and version to determine known vulnerabilities and the appropriate exploits.
Identify application architecture including Web language, WAF, Reverse proxy, Application Server, Backend Database.
Identify if application is behind WAF.
Understand the infrastructure elements interactions, config management for software, backend DB server, WebDAV, FTP in order to identify known vulnerabilities.
Identify default installation file/directory, Handle Server errors (40*,50*), Minimal Privilege, Software logging.

items.testName: Test File Extensions Handling for Sensitive Information
items.description: Find important file, information (.asa, .inc, .sql, zip, tar, pdf, txt, etc).

items.testName: Backup and Unreferenced Files for Sensitive Information
items.description: Check JS source code, comments, cache file, backup file (.old, .bak, .inc, .src) and guessing of filename.

items.testName: Enumerate Infrastructure and Application Admin Interfaces
items.description: Directory and file enumeration, comments and links in source (/admin, /administrator, /backoffice, /backend, etc), alternative server port (Tomcat/8080).
items.tools: Burp Suite, dirb, Dirbuster, fuzzdb, gobuster

items.description: Identify HTTP allowed methods on Web server with OPTIONS. Arbitrary HTTP Methods, HEAD access control bypass and XST.
Identify HSTS header on Web server through HTTP response header. (e.g., using curl to check for 'Strict-Transport-Security').
Analyse permissions allowed from policy files (crossdomain.xml/clientaccesspolicy.xml) and allow-access-from.
Validate the system roles defined within the application by creating a permission matrix.
Verify that identity requirements for user registration are aligned with business and security requirements.
Determine which roles can provision users and what types of accounts they can provision.

items.testName: Testing for Account Enumeration and Guessable User Account
items.description: Check generic login error statements, return codes/parameter values to enumerate valid user IDs.

items.testName: Testing for Weak or unenforced username/password policy
items.description: Validate that account names are not easily guessable.
Evaluate consistency between access policy and guest/training account permissions.
Verify identity requirements for account suspension/resumption.

items.testName: Testing for Credentials Transported over an Encrypted Channel
items.description: Check if credentials are transmitted over HTTPs rather than HTTP.
Test for common default credentials on applications and new accounts.

items.testName: Testing for Weak lock out mechanism
items.description: Evaluate account lockout mechanisms against brute-force password guessing and check the unlock mechanism.

items.testName: Testing for Bypassing Session Management Schema
items.description: Identify session management schema and check for bypassing methods.
Check for secure flag, HttpOnly flag, domain, path and expires attributes in cookies.
Check if the application renews session ID after successful authentication.
Check if session variables are exposed in URLs, logs, or referrer headers.

items.testName: Testing for Cross Site Request Forgery
items.description: Check if the application is vulnerable to CSRF attacks.
Verify proper session termination and token invalidation on logout.
Check if sessions timeout appropriately after periods of inactivity.
Check for session confusion across different application contexts.
Check for directory traversal and local/remote file inclusion vulnerabilities.
Attempt to bypass authorization controls and access restricted resources.
Check for horizontal and vertical privilege escalation vulnerabilities.

items.testName: Testing for Insecure Direct Object References
items.description: Check if the application properly validates access to objects.
Verify that business logic properly validates and handles input data.
Check if malicious requests can be forged to bypass business logic.
Verify data integrity mechanisms in business processes.
Check for timing-based vulnerabilities in business processes.

items.testName: Test Number of Times a Function Can be Used Limits
items.description: Verify proper limits on function usage and rate limiting.

items.testName: Testing for the Circumvention of Work Flows
items.description: Check if application workflows can be bypassed or manipulated.
Verify defenses against application abuse and misuse.

items.testName: Test Upload of Unexpected File Types
items.description: Check file upload functionality for security vulnerabilities.
Attempt to upload malicious files and check execution.

items.testName: Testing for Reflected Cross Site Scripting
items.description: Check for reflected XSS vulnerabilities in input fields.

items.testName: Testing for Stored Cross Site Scripting
items.description: Check for stored XSS vulnerabilities that persist in the application.
Check if the application properly handles different HTTP methods.
Check for HTTP parameter pollution vulnerabilities.
Check for SQL injection vulnerabilities in database interactions.
Check for LDAP injection vulnerabilities.
Check for Object Relational Mapping injection vulnerabilities.
Check for XML injection and XXE vulnerabilities.
Check for Server Side Include injection vulnerabilities.
Check for XPath injection vulnerabilities.
Check for IMAP and SMTP injection vulnerabilities.
Check for code injection vulnerabilities.
Check for local file inclusion vulnerabilities.
Check for remote file inclusion vulnerabilities.
Check for OS command injection vulnerabilities.
Check for buffer overflow vulnerabilities.
Check for vulnerabilities that may manifest later.
Check for HTTP request splitting and smuggling vulnerabilities.
Analyze application error codes for information disclosure.
Check if stack traces reveal sensitive information.

items.testName: Testing for Weak SSL/TLS Ciphers, Insufficient Transport Layer Protection
items.description: Check for weak cryptographic implementations and transport security.
Check for padding oracle attacks in cryptographic implementations.

items.testName: Testing for Sensitive information sent via unencrypted channels
items.description: Verify that sensitive data is properly encrypted in transit.

items.testName: Testing for DOM based Cross Site Scripting
items.description: Check for DOM-based XSS vulnerabilities in client-side code.
Check for unauthorized JavaScript execution vulnerabilities.
Check for HTML injection vulnerabilities.

items.testName: Testing for Client Side URL Redirect
items.description: Check for client-side URL redirection vulnerabilities.
Check for CSS injection vulnerabilities.

items.testName: Testing for Client Side Resource Manipulation
items.description: Check for client-side resource manipulation vulnerabilities.
Check CORS implementation for security issues.
Check for Cross-Site Flashing vulnerabilities in Flash content.
Check for clickjacking vulnerabilities and frame busting.
Check WebSocket implementation for security vulnerabilities.
Check HTML5 web messaging for security issues.
Determine whether sensitive data is stored in local storage.
